Web properties sharing a registered root domain (eTLD+1) frequently run the same tag management infrastructure and tracking stack across subdomains (e.g., `blog.example.com`, `shop.example.com`, and `example.com`), yet previously subdomains were treated as disjoint entities relying purely on hyperlink graph traversal. We extract registered root domains across all hostnames using an extensive public-suffix-aware rule set, estimate empirical conditional tracker distributions from training sister domains, and propagate this high-precision evidence directly as well as through tracker co-occurrence transition dynamics. Coordinate ascent optimization directly calibrates the sister inheritance weights on the holdout validation set to maximize Recall@10 before generating final predictions for all target domains.

nodes.plan: The previous implementation encountered a runtime `NameError` because the SLD co-occurrence feature was defined as `V_cooccur_sld` but referenced in the feature list as `V_sld_cooccur`. To resolve this and maximize the Recall@10 evaluation metric, we fix the variable naming mismatch and decouple neighbor co-occurrence into separate out-neighbor and in-neighbor co-occurrence features (`V_cooccur_out` and `V_cooccur_in`). We also refine the URL category assignment to fall back to the registrable domain (SLD) if the exact hostname is not found, providing category signal to substantially more domains. Finally, we implement multi-pass coordinate ascent optimization on the hold-out validation set to fine-tune feature weights directly for Recall@10, and generate the required submission file.

nodes.plan: An analysis of the multi-relational graph propagation framework reveals that while hyperlink transitions and co-outlink paths provide strong signal, the model treats hostnames as isolated entities and misses critical organizational context: direct outbound links to tracker subdomains (such as `pixel.facebook.net` or `sb.scorecardresearch.com`) fail to match because tracker entries only store specific hostnames, and related subdomains under the same registered root domain (SLD / eTLD+1) cannot inherit shared tag management infrastructure. To address this, we introduce public-suffix-aware registered root domain (SLD) resolution into the pipeline: (1) we resolve tracking services to their registrable root domains (excluding generic hubs) to expand direct tracker hyperlink detection across all associated infrastructure subdomains; (2) we compute empirical Bayes sister-domain tracker distributions ($P(t \mid \text{SLD})$ with companion transition diffusion) to propagate high-confidence tracking stacks across subdomains of the same organization; and (3) we incorporate direct-link cosine affinity diffusion (`dir_cos`) and BM25-IDF co-inlinking (`co_in_idf`) into the coordinate ascent ensemble to optimize Recall@10 on the holdout validation set.
